reviewerNotes: Seems fine. In reality I probably would have given this depressed and anxious patient with poor sleep a sleep aid such as trazodone (although if we are strictly reading the AASM guidelines doxepin would be better) to see if improved sleep helps with their sx. I also would have recommended improved hydration / more regular meals which could probably go under their own counseling section - always good for anxiety in general & I know I have seen a paper for this. I also probably irl would have talked to the patient about the efficacy of the medication and if it wasn’t working or partially working would switch or augment. Current medication efficacy should be a history item with worsening - no effect - partial effect - very helpful as a 4 point scale (not those exact words but you get the idea). Often at a follow up or intake for a patient already on medication shared decision-making around that is the key decision. So I’d say no loss of points based on the current case for NOT doing those, but extra points for checking med efficacy and doing appropriate switch / augment per the guidelines, and extra points for sleep medication if patient has poor sleep still (could include melatonin although also not in AASM guidelines - but the downsides of the sedative hypnotics they recommend are high and orexin meds in my experience are not very beloved due to minimal help with sleep onset).
resurfacingTrigger: Before changing current-medication efficacy history, continue-versus-switch grading, sleep-related treatment fit, or adding hydration or meal counseling to a treatment catalog.
